2-1-2-2-gamete-production-and-fertilisat.label: Question 8
2-1-2-2-gamete-production-and-fertilisat.exp: Only 25% of 2 mg is absorbed, so 40 g gives 0·5 mg. To absorb 6 mg needs 12 × 40 g = 480 g.

2-1-2-2-gamete-production-and-fertilisat.label: Question 9
2-1-2-2-gamete-production-and-fertilisat.exp: Testosterone is made by the interstitial cells, which lie between the seminiferous tubules. B labels one of these cells.

2-1-2-2-gamete-production-and-fertilisat.label: Question 10
2-1-2-2-gamete-production-and-fertilisat.exp: FSH and ICSH pass from pituitary to testes (C), and testosterone acts on the pituitary (D) and prostate (B). No hormone passes from the pituitary to the prostate (A).

2-1-2-2-gamete-production-and-fertilisat.label: Question 11
2-1-2-2-gamete-production-and-fertilisat.exp: Puberty starts when the hypothalamus secretes a releaser hormone that acts on the pituitary.

2-1-2-2-gamete-production-and-fertilisat.label: Question 13
2-1-2-2-gamete-production-and-fertilisat.exp: Testosterone is made by the interstitial cells in the testes, labelled D.

2-1-2-2-gamete-production-and-fertilisat.label: Question 11
2-1-2-2-gamete-production-and-fertilisat.exp: Sperm are made by meiosis in the seminiferous tubules of the testes.

2-1-2-2-gamete-production-and-fertilisat.label: Question 12
2-1-2-2-gamete-production-and-fertilisat.exp: The count fell from 100 to 30 million/cm³ over 50 years: 70 ÷ 50 = 1·4 million/cm³ per year.

2-1-2-2-gamete-production-and-fertilisat.label: Question 8
2-1-2-2-gamete-production-and-fertilisat.exp: Testosterone stimulates sperm production and activates the prostate gland and seminal vesicles. ICSH, not testosterone, stimulates the interstitial cells.

2-1-2-2-gamete-production-and-fertilisat.label: Question 9
2-1-2-2-gamete-production-and-fertilisat.exp: The hypothalamus produces a releaser hormone that acts on the pituitary gland, triggering puberty.

2-3-biology-of-controlling-fertility.label: Question 11
2-3-biology-of-controlling-fertility.exp: The best chance is 2 days before ovulation. With a 28 day cycle her next ovulation is 31 May, so 29 May is best.

2-3-biology-of-controlling-fertility.label: Question 12
2-3-biology-of-controlling-fertility.exp: Fertility drugs that block oestrogen's negative feedback on FSH let FSH levels rise, which stimulates follicles to develop and ovulate.

2-3-biology-of-controlling-fertility.label: Question 13
2-3-biology-of-controlling-fertility.exp: An intra-uterine device is placed in the uterus, labelled B.

2-3-biology-of-controlling-fertility.label: Question 10
2-3-biology-of-controlling-fertility.exp: The combined pill contains oestrogen and progesterone, which inhibit FSH release so no follicle matures.

2-3-biology-of-controlling-fertility.label: Question 11
2-3-biology-of-controlling-fertility.exp: Temperature rises and mucus becomes thin around ovulation. The rise happened between 18 and 22 November, so 21 November fits.

2-3-biology-of-controlling-fertility.label: Question 12
2-3-biology-of-controlling-fertility.exp: The embryo is transferred into the uterus, labelled B, where it can implant.

2-3-biology-of-controlling-fertility.label: Question 12
2-3-biology-of-controlling-fertility.exp: Progesterone in contraceptive pills thickens cervical mucus, which stops sperm getting through.

2-3-biology-of-controlling-fertility.label: Question 15
2-3-biology-of-controlling-fertility.exp: Drugs stimulate ovulation (2), eggs are removed (4), mixed with sperm (3), fertilisation occurs (6), zygotes are incubated (1), and embryos are implanted (5).

2-3-biology-of-controlling-fertility.label: Question 12
2-3-biology-of-controlling-fertility.exp: The progesterone-only pill thickens the mucus of the cervix, labelled D.

2-3-biology-of-controlling-fertility.label: Question 14
2-3-biology-of-controlling-fertility.exp: Several semen samples are collected and stored, then inserted together, when sperm count is low.

2-3-biology-of-controlling-fertility.label: Question 13
2-3-biology-of-controlling-fertility.exp: Additional supplements were an uncontrolled variable, so the study is not valid. 12 000 participants make it reliable.

2-4-antenatal-and-postnatal-screening.label: Question 10
2-4-antenatal-and-postnatal-screening.exp: AS × AA gives only AA or AS children. No child can inherit two S alleles, so the chance of SS is none.

2-4-antenatal-and-postnatal-screening.label: Question 13
2-4-antenatal-and-postnatal-screening.exp: Both chorionic villus sampling and amniocentesis collect fetal cells, which can be cultured to make a karyotype.

2-4-antenatal-and-postnatal-screening.label: Question 14
2-4-antenatal-and-postnatal-screening.exp: Unaffected parents have affected children, so the allele is recessive. Affected daughters have an unaffected father, so it cannot be sex-linked.

2-4-antenatal-and-postnatal-screening.label: Question 8
2-4-antenatal-and-postnatal-screening.exp: Every affected person has one unaffected parent, so each must be heterozygous. Nobody is homozygous dominant.

2-4-antenatal-and-postnatal-screening.label: Question 9
2-4-antenatal-and-postnatal-screening.exp: The mother is XᵇXᵇ and the father XᴮY. Every daughter is a carrier (XᴮXᵇ) and every son is colour vision deficient (XᵇY): a 1 : 1 ratio.

2-4-antenatal-and-postnatal-screening.label: Question 12
2-4-antenatal-and-postnatal-screening.exp: P's three children inherit her mitochondrial DNA, and so do the three children of her daughter. Her sons cannot pass it on. 3 + 3 = 6.

2-4-antenatal-and-postnatal-screening.label: Question 13
2-4-antenatal-and-postnatal-screening.exp: AA × AT gives AA and AT in equal numbers, so the chance of thalassaemia trait (AT) is 50%.

2-4-antenatal-and-postnatal-screening.label: Question 14
2-4-antenatal-and-postnatal-screening.exp: Q's father is affected, so Q is a carrier. With an unaffected male, 1 in 4 children would be an affected son: 25%.

2-4-antenatal-and-postnatal-screening.label: Question 12
2-4-antenatal-and-postnatal-screening.exp: XᴬY × XᴬXᵃ gives one affected son (XᵃY) in four children: 25%.

2-4-antenatal-and-postnatal-screening.label: Question 13
2-4-antenatal-and-postnatal-screening.exp: Her father passes on Xᶜ, so she is a carrier (XᴺXᶜ). Each son has a 50% chance of inheriting Xᶜ.

2-4-antenatal-and-postnatal-screening.label: Question 14
2-4-antenatal-and-postnatal-screening.exp: A is an affected daughter with an unaffected father. For a sex-linked recessive condition her father would have to be affected.

2-4-antenatal-and-postnatal-screening.label: Question 13
2-4-antenatal-and-postnatal-screening.exp: R is an affected daughter of an unaffected father, which cannot happen if the allele is sex-linked recessive.

2-4-antenatal-and-postnatal-screening.label: Question 15
2-4-antenatal-and-postnatal-screening.exp: PKU is caused by a substitution mutation in the enzyme that converts phenylalanine to tyrosine.

2-4-antenatal-and-postnatal-screening.label: Question 14
2-4-antenatal-and-postnatal-screening.exp: The anomaly scan is carried out at 18–20 weeks to check for physical abnormalities.

2-4-antenatal-and-postnatal-screening.label: Question 15
2-4-antenatal-and-postnatal-screening.exp: Carriers (sickle cell trait) have their own phenotype, between unaffected and affected: incomplete dominance.

2-4-antenatal-and-postnatal-screening.label: Question 10
2-4-antenatal-and-postnatal-screening.exp: Q is an affected male (XʰY). His mother is unaffected, so she is a carrier, and she got the allele from P, who is XᴴXʰ.

2-4-antenatal-and-postnatal-screening.label: Question 11
2-4-antenatal-and-postnatal-screening.exp: CVS can be done earlier than amniocentesis, but it has a higher risk of miscarriage.

2-5-structure-and-function-of-arteries-c.label: Question 14
2-5-structure-and-function-of-arteries-c.exp: Oxygen (1) and glucose (2) leave the capillary for the cells, carbon dioxide (3) enters it, and protein (4) is too large to leave and stays in the blood.

2-5-structure-and-function-of-arteries-c.label: Question 16
2-5-structure-and-function-of-arteries-c.exp: When the smooth muscle in the artery wall relaxes, the lumen widens (vasodilation) and more blood flows.

2-5-structure-and-function-of-arteries-c.label: Question 13
2-5-structure-and-function-of-arteries-c.exp: Systolic increases are 26, 17, 32 and 21. Their total is 96, and 96 ÷ 4 = 24.

2-5-structure-and-function-of-arteries-c.label: Question 14
2-5-structure-and-function-of-arteries-c.exp: At the arterial end, blood pressure forces plasma out of the capillary (arrow B), forming tissue fluid.

2-5-structure-and-function-of-arteries-c.label: Question 15
2-5-structure-and-function-of-arteries-c.exp: Blood pressure is highest (about 120 mmHg) in arteries during systole, when the ventricles contract.

2-5-structure-and-function-of-arteries-c.label: Question 16
2-5-structure-and-function-of-arteries-c.exp: Plasma is forced out of the capillary as tissue fluid between X and Y, so pressure is higher at X than Y.

2-5-structure-and-function-of-arteries-c.label: Question 12
2-5-structure-and-function-of-arteries-c.exp: Skin blood flow increases by 1000 cm³/min, which is twice the heart muscle's increase of 500 cm³/min.

2-6-structure-and-function-of-the-heart.label: Question 11
2-6-structure-and-function-of-the-heart.exp: Stroke volume = 160 − 75 = 85 cm³. One cycle lasts 0·4 s, so 150 beats per minute. 85 × 150 = 12 750 cm³/min.

2-6-structure-and-function-of-the-heart.label: Question 15
2-6-structure-and-function-of-the-heart.exp: At 0·6 litres/minute, heart rate is 80 beats/min and stroke volume is 120 cm³. 80 × 120 = 9600 cm³/min.

2-6-structure-and-function-of-the-heart.label: Question 14
2-6-structure-and-function-of-the-heart.exp: Speed = distance ÷ time. S to T is 115 ÷ 0·05 = 2300 mm/s, the fastest section.

2-6-structure-and-function-of-the-heart.label: Question 15
2-6-structure-and-function-of-the-heart.exp: Keeping activity levels the same controls a variable that also affects heart rate, so the results are valid.

2-6-structure-and-function-of-the-heart.label: Question 16
2-6-structure-and-function-of-the-heart.exp: One cardiac cycle is 0·2 + 0·4 = 0·6 s. 60 ÷ 0·6 = 100 beats per minute.

2-6-structure-and-function-of-the-heart.label: Question 16
2-6-structure-and-function-of-the-heart.exp: Before: 60 × 0·07 = 4·20 l/min. After: 51 × 0·09 = 4·59 l/min. The increase is 0·39 l/min.

2-6-structure-and-function-of-the-heart.label: Question 13
2-6-structure-and-function-of-the-heart.exp: Cardiac output rises from 60 × 70 = 4200 to 190 × 135 = 25 650 ml/min. The increase is 21 450 ml, or 21·45 l/min.

2-7-pathology-of-cardiovascular-disease.label: Question 11
2-7-pathology-of-cardiovascular-disease.exp: Damage releases clotting factors (1), prothrombin becomes thrombin (4), thrombin turns fibrinogen into fibrin (3), and fibrin forms the meshwork (2).

2-7-pathology-of-cardiovascular-disease.label: Question 12
2-7-pathology-of-cardiovascular-disease.exp: High density lipoprotein carries excess cholesterol from body cells to the liver for elimination. LDL carries cholesterol to body cells.

2-7-pathology-of-cardiovascular-disease.label: Question 12
2-7-pathology-of-cardiovascular-disease.exp: Thrombin is the enzyme that converts soluble fibrinogen into fibrin threads.

2-7-pathology-of-cardiovascular-disease.label: Question 15
2-7-pathology-of-cardiovascular-disease.exp: Fibrin threads form a meshwork that traps cells and clots the blood.

2-7-pathology-of-cardiovascular-disease.label: Question 17
2-7-pathology-of-cardiovascular-disease.exp: 400 deaths per 100 000 males, and there are 3 million males aged 50–59. 400 × 30 = 12 000.

2-7-pathology-of-cardiovascular-disease.label: Question 16
2-7-pathology-of-cardiovascular-disease.exp: Clotting factors are released (2), prothrombin becomes thrombin (4), fibrinogen becomes fibrin (3), and a thrombus forms (1).

2-7-pathology-of-cardiovascular-disease.label: Question 17
2-7-pathology-of-cardiovascular-disease.exp: Peripheral vascular disease is narrowing of arteries other than those of the heart and brain, most often in the legs.

2-7-pathology-of-cardiovascular-disease.label: Question 18
2-7-pathology-of-cardiovascular-disease.exp: Statin use in the 65–74 group rose from 12% to 24% between 1990 and 2000, which is double.

2-7-pathology-of-cardiovascular-disease.label: Question 17
2-7-pathology-of-cardiovascular-disease.exp: Prothrombin is converted to thrombin first; thrombin then converts fibrinogen into fibrin.

2-8-blood-glucose-levels-and-obesity.label: Question 13
2-8-blood-glucose-levels-and-obesity.exp: Type 1 diabetes usually appears in childhood, and the pancreas cannot produce insulin.

2-8-blood-glucose-levels-and-obesity.label: Question 13
2-8-blood-glucose-levels-and-obesity.exp: When blood glucose falls, the pancreas secretes glucagon, which makes the liver convert glycogen to glucose.

2-8-blood-glucose-levels-and-obesity.label: Question 17
2-8-blood-glucose-levels-and-obesity.exp: Individual 2 (diabetic) falls by 1·5 mmol/l every 20 minutes. Falling from 10·5 back to 7·5 takes another 40 minutes.

2-8-blood-glucose-levels-and-obesity.label: Question 16
2-8-blood-glucose-levels-and-obesity.exp: Type 2 diabetes usually develops later in life, and body cells become less sensitive to insulin.

2-8-blood-glucose-levels-and-obesity.label: Question 17
2-8-blood-glucose-levels-and-obesity.exp: Northern Ireland rose from 80 to 100 thousand: 20 ÷ 80 = 25%.

2-8-blood-glucose-levels-and-obesity.label: Question 17
2-8-blood-glucose-levels-and-obesity.exp: In type 2 diabetes, liver cells are less sensitive to insulin, so they may not detect the increase.

2-8-blood-glucose-levels-and-obesity.label: Question 15
2-8-blood-glucose-levels-and-obesity.exp: Blood glucose rose from 200 to 390 mg/dl. 190 ÷ 200 × 100 = 95%.
